title: A kilometre-long crack runs under homes on the Tláhuac / Valle de Chalco line
caption: News photo and story. A crack about 1.5 m wide crosses Eje 10 Sur at a petrol station and reaches the corner of Luciano Navarrete and El Pípila, through the colonias San Miguel, Barrio de la Concepción and Santa Catarina. Cars slow to cross it and houses tilt. In Valle de Chalco, Lourdes Baltazar's house on Calle Rafael Núñez lost a wall in the 2017 quake; her patio sank until the family 'built steps', and her neighbour has had no water for six months because the pipe broke.
loc_method: research: Calle Luciano Navarrete x Calle El Pípila, Santa Catarina Yecahuízotl, Tláhuac, CDMX; continuing under Calle Rafael Núñez, Valle de Chalco (Edomex)

title: Sierra de Santa Catarina: the volcanic ridge that doesn't sink
caption: Photo: the line of volcanic cones of the Sierra de Santa Catarina, taken from the summit of Cerro de la Estrella, looking SE over the Iztapalapa lowland (2005). An alternative image, 'Volcan Yuhualixqui visto desde San Pedro Tláhuac' (ProtoplasmaKid, CC BY-SA 4.0, 2022, GPS 19.269241,-99.005417), looks north at the same ridge from the sinking Tláhuac lake-bed. NISAR reads -13.2 cm at that camera position (window -16.5 to -12.4). One frame, both sides of the boundary.
loc_method: research: Sierra de Santa Catarina (volcanoes Yuhualixqui, Xaltepec, Tetecón, Tecuauhtzin, Guadalupe, La Caldera), Iztapalapa/Tláhuac

title: The Metropolitan Cathedral, sinking unevenly into the lake-bed
caption: The cathedral's facade and bell towers from the Zócalo (2024). English Wikipedia: 'The cathedral, along with the rest of the city, has been sinking into the lakebed from the day it was built'. In the late 20th century parts of the complex were sinking at different rates and the bell towers were tilting dangerously. Underpinning work 'corrected the tilting towers and ensured that the cathedral will sink uniformly'. It was placed on the World Monuments Fund's 100 Most Endangered Sites list.
credit: ProtoplasmaKid, via Wikimedia Commons; text: en.wikipedia 'Mexico City Metropolitan Cathedral'
